title: Stop achievementsOverviewProvider and _pointConfigDataProvider writing to Drift/SharedPreferences and pushing to Firestore from inside FutureProvider build
rule: SM-2 (provider build is pure: no writes/requests/side effects)
why: Both providers exist to compute a read-only view model (achievements list / per-track point config rows), but their build functions mutate persisted state (SharedPreferences milestone config, Drift PointConfigs rows) and push a network sync write as an unguarded side effect of simply being watched. Riverpod rebuilds these providers on every dependency change (achievementsOverviewProvider re-runs on every completionCommittedProvider tick; _pointConfigDataProvider re-runs whenever activeTracksProvider emits) -- so opening the achievements screen or the point-settings screen can silently trigger writes and a Firestore push purely from reading state, with no user action and no guard against concurrent/duplicate invocation. This also makes both providers impossible to unit test as pure read logic without a working sync facade and DB write path.
recommendation: Move the strip-stock-templates / seed-default-configs mutations out of the read providers into an explicit one-shot action (invoked once from a screen lifecycle hook or a dedicated Notifier method with SM-4-safe mounted checks), leaving the FutureProviders as pure reads.
acceptance_criteria: achievementsOverviewProvider's build function performs no writes; a separate, explicitly-invoked action performs stripStockTemplateMilestones + push
_pointConfigDataProvider's build function performs no writes; seeding defaults happens in a separate action
A ProviderContainer.test() test watches each read provider twice and asserts the mutation/sync-push call count is 0 (or exactly 1, deliberately) rather than growing with rebuilds
